$comment: Known divergences between the two 44-check engines, pinned to the canonical hash of BOTH sides. kind=intentional: the copies differ by design (transport, output envelope). kind=debt: a fix landed in route.ts and was never ported; porting it and deleting the entry is the goal. See scripts/source-drift.mjs.

fn:checkDesignMdSpec.why: Transport, with the verdict logic now ALIGNED (measured 2026-09-30). route.ts fetches via safeFetch (throws on failure -> its own SKIP) and engine.ts via httpsFetch with an SSRF guard (returns an outcome object, so the equivalent SKIP happens at the length check). Every verdict branch now carries the same status: SKIP not-served, WARN no-frontmatter, MANUAL linter-unavailable, FAIL lint errors, WARN lint warnings, PASS linted clean, WARN lint threw. The linter-unavailable branch was PASS in engine.ts (asserted validation that never ran), then WARN (2026-09-30), which charged the scored site for a package missing from the runtime: the npm CLI scored www.designesy.org 96.1 against the API's 98. Both copies moved to MANUAL, weight 0, on 2026-10-06 (score 0.5.1). Both copies pass a caught error's text through the shared sanitizeErrorText before it reaches the detail (2026-10-10, score 0.7.1: 0.7.0 echoed the CLI user's npm cache path). Only the fetch wiring differs, so this stays baselined as transport rather than debt.

fn:emitCanonical.why: Output envelope, measured 2026-09-30. The payload is IDENTICAL: every top-level key route.ts emits except `receipt` and `generatedAt` is present in engine.ts with the same value expression, verified by normalized comparison. route.ts additionally attaches buildReceipt(...) and takes a retrievedAt Date for generatedAt; the standalone package has no receipt concept and stamps new Date(). Same split as emitDesignesy.

fn:emitDesignesy.why: Output envelope. route.ts attaches a receipt (buildReceipt) for the HTTP API and strips the internal retrievedAt; the package returns the result as-is.

fn:fetchPageResilient.why: Transport. route.ts uses fetch via fetchCssSingleDetailed and reports a typed failure reason; engine.ts uses node:https with an SSRF guard (isValidUrl, safeLookup).
